query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Alloying equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with Mo will improve its oxygen resistance by forming a protective oxide layer.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state
generation.conditions: Exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective oxide layer
generation.mechanism: The addition of Mo will promote the formation of a stable and dense oxide layer, reducing the oxidation rate and improving the alloy's oxygen resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance, as evidenced by reduced oxidation rate and increased protection against pesting
generation.boundary: Temperature: 800 °C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure time: 5 hours, Loading: No external loading
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of oxide layer formation and its effectiveness in improving oxygen resistance is uncertain and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the oxidation resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy with and without Mo addition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with Mo addition shows no significant improvement in oxygen resistance compared to the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Paper card. Question: What are the individual effects of Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr on the microstructure and mechanical properties (yield strength, ductility, and elevated-temperature performance) of equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr refractory high-entropy alloys?. System: Equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr and its five sub-alloys created by the subtraction method: HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi. Processing: Vacuum-arc melting of 99.9 wt.% (99.99 wt.% for Ti) pure elements stacked by melting point, re-melted at least four times, and solidified in a water-cool copper mold. Test conditions: Compression tests at room temperature, 800 °C, 1000 °C, 1200 °C, and 1400 °C; crosshead speed 0.36 mm/min (strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹); cylindrical samples 3.6 mm diameter x 6 mm height. Findings: HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy yield strength was 1512 MPa at room temperature and 556 MPa at 1200 °C.; HfMoTaTiZr (Nb removed) showed the highest room temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa
